Matt Pierce's June Newsletter Indiana ranks 45th for support of public education, Interim Study Committees and more. Rep. Matt Pierce Jun 30, 2026 Share Welcome to my monthly newsletter, where I provide legislative updates as your state representative for House District 61. Please reach out to me at h61@iga.in.gov if you have any comments, questions, or concerns. Everyone Should Be Welcome in Indiana Indiana is home to nearly 7 million people who worship in different ways and raise families of every shape. At the start of this month, Indiana’s leaders spent time casting judgment on families and faiths that don’t resemble their own. Lt. Gov. Micah Beckwith told Hoosiers it is acceptable to hate again, characterizing our Muslim neighbors as jihadists. The same neighbors are raising their kids and building their lives in our communities. On the first day of June, Gov. Mike Braun declared that a biological nuclear family is “God’s design,” brushing aside single parents, blended families, adoptive families, grandparents raising grandchildren, and households led by two moms or two dads. Our communities are made stronger by the diversity of experiences, traditions, and families that call Indiana home. Every family building a safe, loving home deserves dignity and respect. Hoosier hospitality has always meant taking care of your neighbors and welcoming people as they are. Time spent by the Braun-Beckwith administration policing private lives is time not spent on the issues that matter. F amilies are stretched thin, paying for the basics necessary to maintain their households. Health care, child care and affordable housing are beyond the reach of too many. Hoosiers did not ask for a lecture on who belongs here. They want help making ends meet. I choose to represent every Hoosier family and every faith, not just those approved by Governor Braun or Lt. Governor Beckwith . Indiana Ranks 45th for Public Education Support The Network for Public Education released its 2026 national report card , and Indiana received an “F” ranking. Indiana ranked 45th in the nation for legislative support for public education. This data confirms what those of us who have been fighting for public education in the state legislature have been saying for years. This is a direct consequence of the Statehouse Republicans’ support for voucher s for private schools . Each year, Statehouse Republicans have expanded eligibility for vouchers, siphoning money away from public schools . Vouchers are now universal. Any family, regardless of wealth, can receive a state-funded voucher of $6,100 to $8,300 to cover the cost of private school. There is no income eligibility limit. A billionaire qualifies for a taxpayer-funded voucher. Privatization and disinvestment in our public schools go hand in hand. In the 2024-25 school year, Indiana spent close to $497 million on vouchers , a $58 million increase from the prior school year. The two-year state budget spends more than $1.2 billion on the program. Each dollar in the budget for the voucher program is a dollar less for our public schools. Our communities are feeling the impact. NPE’s report notes Indiana’s poor marks on teacher-student ratios, counselor-student ratios, and the inability to attract prospective teachers to the profession. Each of these is a symptom of chronic underfunding. This report card gives Indiana a failing grade. Around 90% of students choose public schools. As the state legislature enters the next budget cycle, I will advocate for Indiana’s public school system, which serves the majority of our students. My Interim Study Committees Between legislative sessions, interim study committees are assigned topics to study for possible legislation in the coming session. Committees have the opportunity to consider specific issues, analyze recent studies, and decide if legislation should be recommended for consideration by the entire Indiana General Assembly. I am serving on these interim study committees: Artificial Intelligence Task Force Interim Study Committee on Energy, Utilities and Telecommunications Interim Study Committee on Corrections and Criminal Code But I only expect one of these committees will meet. Many of the study committees will not meet this year because they are assigned no topics to study. Republican leaders appear to prefer avoiding talk about challenges facing our state in an election year rather than giving legislators and the public a platform to demand that problems be addressed. The following committees were not assigned any topics to study: Agriculture And Natural Resources Commerce And Economic Development Elections Energy, Utilities, And Telecommunications Environmental Affairs Government Public Safety And Military Affairs Public Policy These task forces and committees created by law were also denied any study topics: Probate Code Study Committee Health Care Cost Oversight Task Force Artificial Intelligence Task Force Child Welfare Task Force Guardianship Code Revision Task Force You can find a full list of topics the legislature is studying here .
